summary: There are many machines on the Moon and Mars that have been left behind after completing their missions. Although we cannot bring most of them back to Earth, we can still learn from their discoveries and remember their stories. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we developed The Silent Explorers, an interactive website dedicated to four of these machines. Our project brings together the history and science behind their missions while also looking at space exploration from a different perspective. We also added voice narration to make the information accessible to people who have difficulty reading. We believe that understanding past missions is just as important as following new ones. Every machine sent into space has helped us gain knowledge and prepare for future missions. With The Silent Explorers, we want to give these machines the attention they deserve and share their stories with a new generation of space enthusiasts.
details: We created a website called The Silent Explorers. It has different sections where users can explore the machines left on the Moon and Mars. Each machine has its own mission profile with photographs, historical information and scientific achievements. Users can choose which machine they want to explore and learn about it at their own pace. We researched when the machines were launched, what their missions were, what they discovered and how their missions ended. We also wrote fictional stories from the perspective of each machine to make the website more interesting. We thought it would be creative to imagine what these machines would say if they could tell their own stories. Along with these stories, we included a timeline showing important events and a quiz where users can test what they have learned.We used HTML, CSS and JavaScript to build the website, Visual Studio Code to write the code and GitHub Pages to publish it. We used ChatGPT to help us with coding, debugging and some of the written content. We also used NASA resources to gather scientific and historical information.During the development process, we considered the accuracy of the information, the visual design and how easily users could navigate the website. We wanted the website to be accessible and understandable even for people who do not know much about space. To make it more accessible, we added small speaker buttons next to individual texts using the browser's Web Speech API. By clicking these buttons, users can listen to mission information, stories, timeline events and even quiz questions instead of reading them.Our aim was to create something that people could enjoy exploring while learning about the history of space exploration. We also wanted the information to be easy to understand, especially for students. Through our project, we hope to increase interest in space exploration and help people remember the machines that made many of today's discoveries possible.
